description:
RE-TESTED at main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83
(2026-09-02).

## Goal

A source declaration must not be allowed to claim a type spelling whose meaning
is owned by FZ's builtin type syntax. Reject the declaration at its `@type`
span, before it is bound into the namespace or published as `TypeDefined`.

The rejection must be a user-facing diagnostic. No builtin collision may be
silently accepted, and no malformed collision may escape as an
`internal/post-resolution-leftover` diagnostic at `<generated>`.

## Current reproducer: identifier-shaped builtin

```fz
defmodule M do
  @type list :: {atom, integer}
  @spec f(list) :: integer
  fn f(x), do: 1
end

fn main() do
  dbg(M.f({:a, 2}))
end
```

At a3a9761d1, run, interp, and build all reject the call rather than the
declaration:

```text
error[spec/violation]: call to `f/1` violates its @spec for arguments ({:a, int})
  --> repro.fz:7:7
   |
 7 |   dbg(M.f({:a, 2}))
   |       ^^^^^^^^^^^^ no declared @spec accepts these arguments
```

An otherwise unused declaration compiles and exits 0:

```fz
defmodule M do
  @type list :: {atom, integer}
end

fn main(), do: 0
```

A parameterized declaration has the same defect:

```fz
defmodule M do
  @type list(t) :: {t, integer}
  @spec f(list(atom)) :: integer
  fn f(x), do: 1
end

fn main() do
  dbg(M.f({:a, 2}))
end
```

It produces the same `spec/violation`, because builtin lookup matches the name
before considering the namespace binding.

Elixir 1.19.4 rejects both declarations at their source:

```text
type list/0 is a built-in type and it cannot be redefined
type list/1 is a built-in type and it cannot be redefined
```

## Current mechanism

- `source_publish.rs:553-582` parses every decoded `TypeAliasDecl`, binds its
  name as `NamespaceSymbol::Type`, and appends it to `pending_types` without
  checking builtin ownership.
- `source_publish.rs:1684-1696` asks `reference_type` for every named type
  expression. Because `list` was bound, a later spec records the inert alias as
  a real `TypeDefined` dependency.
- `resolve.rs:390-406` classifies an unqualified name by calling
  `find_constructor` first. The registry's `list` entry therefore wins before
  `reference_type` can return the user alias.
- The dependency walk and resolver consequently disagree: the contract waits
  on the user alias but resolves the spelling as builtin `list(any)` or
  `list(T)`.

This is name ownership, not an arity-only collision. `@type list(t)` must also
be rejected.

## The nil exception the previous ticket missed

`nil` is listed in `CONSTRUCTORS`, but it does not currently travel through the
same parsing or resolution path as the identifier-shaped constructors.

```fz
defmodule M do
  @type nil :: atom
end

fn main(), do: 0
```

Current FZ output:

```text
error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: nested module body read failed:
expected type-alias name after `@type`, got Nil
  --> <generated>
```

`quoted_surface.rs:428-443` accepts only `Tok::Upper` or `Tok::Ident` as an
alias head, while the lexer emits `Tok::Nil`. In type expressions,
`TypeExpr::Nil` resolves directly at `resolve.rs:338`, so it does not call
`find_constructor`; the `nil` entry in `CONSTRUCTORS` is unreachable through
that path.

Elixir also rejects `@type nil :: atom`, reporting it as an invalid type
specification. FZ must likewise report a source-owned user error, not an
internal generated-source failure.

## Required work

- Establish one authoritative answer for whether an `@type` head is owned by
  builtin type syntax. Do not add a second manually synchronized reserved-name
  list.
- Reject identifier-shaped builtin declarations before namespace binding,
  pending-type publication, or `TypeDefined` production:
  `bool`, `integer`, `float`, `cpointer`, `binary`, `atom`, `any`, `never`,
  `utf8`, `pid`, `ref`, `list`, `resource`, and `map`.
- Handle the literal-token spelling `nil` explicitly at the source-surface
  boundary so it receives the same quality of user-facing, source-spanned
  rejection.
- Reconcile the unreachable `nil` registry entry: either route builtin
  ownership through a representation that genuinely covers it or remove the
  dead constructor entry while retaining `TypeExpr::Nil` as the sole
  resolution owner.
- Do not “fix” only `collect_type_refs`. Skipping the dependency would still
  leave an accepted declaration whose spelling can never denote that
  declaration.

## Decidable checks

- The `list/0` reproducer reports a builtin-type declaration error at the
  `@type` line on run, interp, and build; it never reaches `spec/violation`.
- The `list/1` reproducer receives the same declaration-time rejection.
- Every identifier-shaped builtin listed above is rejected by the same
  authoritative collision policy.
- `@type nil :: atom` produces a user-facing diagnostic at its real source
  span; stderr contains neither `internal/post-resolution-leftover` nor
  `<generated>`.
- A rejected declaration creates no namespace type binding, pending type, or
  `TypeDefined` fact.
- Existing non-builtin aliases remain valid, including:
  - `fixtures2/00079_type_aliases_in_module.fz`
  - `fixtures2/00091_spec_resolves_local_types.fz`
- Existing builtin resolution and arity tests remain green.
- Full library and fixture matrix pass with no new controlled warnings.
title: Reject builtin @type declarations as user errors; nil currently fails internally
